To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

N-methyl-D-Aspartate receptor antagonism increases the protein stability of 4-3-3eta, which in turn causes a shift in GABAAergic signaling from opening Kir3 channels to increasing calcium signals and mammalian Target Of Rapamycin activity.
the GABAB receptor signaling pathway shifts to a resting state calcium increase in the dendrite, and this is mediated by a change in 14-3eta stability.

the N-methyl-D-aspate receptor (N-MDAR) antagonist Ro-25-6891, acting as a rapid-acting antidepressant (RAAD), increases the expression of the GABABR adaptor 14-3eta and decreases the GABAB-R/GIRK3 coupling in the hippocampus, which is essential for RAAD efficacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the cellular and molecular changes underlying the rapid antidepressant effects of NMDAR antagonism.
the mechanisms by which antidepressant medications work and how the molecular mechanisms of these drugs can be used to treat depression.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the efficacy of rapid acting antidepressants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
14-3eta is required for the antidepressant effects of rapid acting NMDA receptor antagonists and the antidepressant effects are mediated by a shift in GABAA receptor signaling to calcium signaling.
the shift from GABA-B to GABAB signaling requires the loss of GABAR-B/GIRK3 channel signaling mediated by 14.3-3η.
NMDA receptors (NMDARs) regulate the GABABR-GIRK pathway through the 14-3 protein 14- 3-3η to modulate synaptic function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shift in the GABABR pathway requires a loss of activity of the GABABRs-GIRK channel interaction mediated by 14.3-3eta.

NMDA receptor antagonists cause a shift in GABAA signaling, from opening inwardly-rectifying potassium channels to increasing resting dendritiic calcium signal and mammaliam target of rapamycin activity.
NMDAR antagonism increases 14-3 protein stability, which in turn decouples GABAR signaling from Kir channels and promotes GABAR signaling to increase calcium signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular mechanisms that underlie rapid antidepressant efficacy are beginning to be elucidated.
the shift in the signaling of the GABABR to Kir3 channels is critical to the efficacy of rapid acting antidepressants.
14-3eta is required for NMDA receptor antagonists to work as antidepressants.
